newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Bullion cuts ground from under SAfrica gold shares.
newsitem.headline: Bullion cuts ground from under SAfrica gold shares.

text.p: Bullion's decline to 12-year lows hacked nearly four percent off South African gold shares in the first 15 minutes of trade on Friday.
In later morning trade the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's All-Gold index recovered slightly to 959.4 points by 0936 GMT.
But dealers and portfolio managers said clouds were massing on gold shares' horizon and the gloom could drag the index as far down as the 850-800 point level in the near future.

"This unbelieveable decline in the gold price is having a disastrous effect on (profit) margins which are already low. (The mines) are taking an enormous amount of pain," said Grahame Graham-Parker, general manager of Infinity Asset Management.

"The gold index looks as if it's heading to the 850 to 800 level. Besides this unbelievable decline (in the gold price) the fundamental picture is not looking that great either. There is nothing on the immediate horizon to chase investors into gold."
The majority of gold mine shares on the JSE hit year lows in Monday morning trade before recovering slightly.

"The fact that it has fallen... took the market by surprise and might influence other people to get out of the market," said David Shapiro, a director at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Marginal mining specialist Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd sank to a new year low of 19 rand before recovering to 19.50 rand from its previous close of 20 rand.
"Marginal companies must show losses at the current gold price," said Dave Giese at stockbrokerage Smith Borkum.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's long-time beleaguered Freegold, the world's biggest gold producer, fell four percent to 23.45 rand.
Worst-hit appeared to be Gencor Ltd's Evander which lost more than eight percent to 17 rand.
Gencor itself saw large volumes of trade with 762,000 shares changing hands so far.
But overall, volumes on the gold board were fairly thin, dealers said.
"The gold market is scrappily traded," one dealer said.
"It's almost as though the market is frozen in horror at the price fall," another dealer said.
The gold price slumped to a 12-year low late Thursday on Australian central bank gold sales and remained vulnerable to further losses, dealers and analysts in London said.
It was last bid at $324.90 an ounce.
Spot gold in New York on Thursday night hit its lowest levels since early December 1985 when gold was recovering from the low of $281 an ounce seen in February 1985.

But one portfolio manager who asked not to be identified said bullion had been looking frail for weeks and this recent slide, although a shock, would likely not have too much more of an impact on the jaded gold share market.

"I've said it before and I'll say it again, there is no future in golds. Yes, today is a good day to get out of golds, but yesterday would have been a better day, and the day before, and so on," he said.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
